issues.title: Distinct HT partitioned on group hash
issues.hypothesis: q16 does count(DISTINCT ps_suppkey) GROUP BY brand,type,size, with about 64K estimated groups. The distinct radix HT partitions on hash(G,x), so every distinct partition holds pieces of every group. Distinct finalize then re-sinks each partition into the main HT, and each task touches nearly all groups. That is a large re-aggregation plus a combine. A prior run on this codebase spliced hash(G) into the radix bits [36,48) of the distinct HT hash and measured q16 -12..-13% twice, and -11% on a later re-implementation.
issues.plan: In radix_partitioned_hashtable.cpp/.hpp add a member (e.g. partition_prefix_count = number of leading group columns) on RadixPartitionedHashTable. In Sink, when it is set, hash the full key, compute hash(first prefix cols), and replace bits [36,48) (the RadixPartitioning MAX_RADIX_BITS mask region) with those bits of the group hash. Call a pre-hashed AddChunk overload and keep the sink_count update inside it, so the adaptivity logic still fires. In physical_hash_aggregate.cpp, when distinct radix tables are built for a grouped aggregate with estimated_cardinality >= 4096, set the prefix count to the number of main group columns, and skip TryAddCompressedGroups in that mode. Distinct finalize is unchanged: each partition now holds whole groups.
issues.expected_gain: q16 -10..-13%. Other count(DISTINCT) GROUP BY templates gain a few %.
issues.generality: Any grouped aggregate with DISTINCT aggregates over many groups. Ungrouped DISTINCT is unaffected (gated). A skewed group could unbalance partitions, and low-group-count queries are gated off by the estimate.
issues.risk: Medium-low. The hash only affects partitioning, so correctness holds as long as the same hash is used consistently for equality probing in the distinct HT: the full hash still decides the slot, only the radix bits are replaced. Test spilling with a low memory_limit.

issues.title: Semi-join RHS-aware estimate + HAVING selectivity
issues.hypothesis: q18 IN (SELECT l_orderkey ... GROUP BY HAVING sum>300): the SEMI case in CardinalityEstimator::CalculateUpdatedDenom (cardinality_estimator.cpp:268) uses left.denom*5 and ignores the RHS size, and relation_manager gives the HAVING filter no selectivity. The optimizer therefore over-estimates the orders⋈subquery result and keeps customer on the build side. A prior run measured q18 -7..-8% with both changes, and either alone did nothing.
issues.plan: cardinality_estimator.cpp CalculateUpdatedDenom SEMI: use selectivity = max(DEFAULT_SEMI_ANTI_SELECTIVITY, tdom/rhs_cardinality). In relation_manager.cpp (near l.495), apply an extra 0.2 to the estimate of an aggregate relation that has a HAVING (filter over aggregate) above it. Verify with EXPLAIN that q18's customer join flips.
issues.generality: IN/EXISTS subqueries with selective RHS (HAVING, filters). Other join orders can change, so check q04/q21/q20-like semi joins.
issues.risk: Medium: it changes join orders broadly for semi joins.

output.memory:
## Memory (gen1)

## State
- r1: E0001 JoinDependentFilterRule before DistributivityRule ACCEPTED: q19 -46%, geomean -4.2%.
- r2: E0002 contains()/LIKE length-aware selectivity ACCEPTED: q09 -37%, geomean -3.9%.
- r3: E0003 Perfect HJ RIGHT v2 ACCEPTED: q13 -18..-20%. Large range (up to 4M) is allowed only for RIGHT joins; for INNER it regressed q14 +52% and q18 +13% (serial perfect build, no BF).
- r4: E0004 substring prefilter (ColumnData::Filter) RETIRED. q13 -7.7% (needed -13.8%). A good idea that fell short of the bar; retry it bundled with FSST batched decode.
- r5: E0005 BF on first key of multi-key HJ ACCEPTED: q09 -18..-22%.
- r6: E0006 join key-set range filter through compress projs ACCEPTED: q18 -6..-9%.
- r7: E0007 exact key-bitmap BF ACCEPTED: q03 -18%, q04 -20%, q09 -12%, q16 -6%, geomean -4.7%. Best 1.178x.
- r8: E0008 exact BF through CM offset RETIRED: q09 -3.9% official (needed -8.6%). Overlaps with E0006/E0007. Don't retry alone.
- r9: E0009 large perfect HA (22 bits) + parallel combine/source RETIRED: q13 -20%, but the official bench had q16 +14% and q18 +7.8%, geomean -0.3%. The implementer called q16/q18 noise on re-run, so the regression may be real or may be noise. q18's 15M-group agg on orderkey is beyond 22 bits, so it is probably not directly affected. Retry only with a runtime fallback (allocate a thread-local table lazily once N rows are seen) and with confirmation that q16/q18 do not take the new path (EXPLAIN shows PERFECT_HASH_GROUP_BY?).
- r10 DISPATCHED: distinct HT partitioned on group hash (q16 prior -12%). Also filed: semi-join RHS-aware estimate + HAVING (q18 prior -8%), the next candidate.
- Claude auto-memory (~/.claude/.../memory) holds results from a PREVIOUS evolve run on this same codebase/workload. Treat them as strong measured priors, not as already-landed code.

## Profile snapshot (r9): q18 647, q13 644, q09 537, q04 269, q05 266, q17 232, q08 227 ms. Geomean 243.7ms.

## Prior-run wins to port, in rough priority order (gain / risk)
1-8. DONE or tried.
9. Semi-join RHS-aware estimate (filed r10): CalculateUpdatedDenom SEMI at cardinality_estimator.cpp:268, and the HAVING change in relation_manager.cpp ~l.495.
10. Distinct HT on group hash (r10 dispatched).
11. OR-of-ranges as ExpressionFilter, dense mask eval: q19 -7..-11%.
12. FSST batched decode (q13 -4..-7%), possibly combined with the substring prefilter retry.
13. E0007 follow-ups: exact BF for IS NOT DISTINCT FROM (q18 RIGHT_SEMI); parallel perfect HJ build.
- q04/q03/q05/q08 are not yet analysed in this run; profile them after the ports run out.

## Known dead ends (prior run)
- HJ prefetch, agg run-collapse, in-place finalize, FSST heap reuse, dictionary filter, scan filter cost ordering, early HT grow, sparse perfect HJ, bitpacking select, BF on sparse perfect HJ, hashed BF through CM offset: all ~0% or worse.

## Codebase facts
- Rule registration order lives in src/optimizer/optimizer.cpp.
- Scan-filter cardinality: RelationStatisticsHelper::InspectTableFilter.
- ColumnData::Filter = Scan + ColumnSegment::FilterSelection. enable_fsst_vectors defaults to false.
- Perfect HJ gates: perfect_hash_join_executor.cpp CanDoPerfectHashJoin; join_filter_pushdown_optimizer.cpp computes min/max.
- BF pushdown: physical_hash_join.cpp JoinFilterPushdownInfo::FinalizeFilters → PushBloomFilter; TrySetExactBloomFilter; exact fill in JoinHashTable::Finalize.
- JoinFilterPushdownColumn: include/duckdb/execution/operator/join/join_filter_pushdown.hpp. CM functions: compress_integral.cpp.
- Perfect HA: plan_aggregate.cpp CanUsePerfectHashAggregate (perfect_ht_threshold).
- Distinct agg: physical_hash_aggregate.cpp distinct_data->radix_tables; RadixPartitionedHashTable::Sink at radix_partitioned_hashtable.cpp:548.
- OptionalFilter is evaluated once per row group or segment; SelectivityOptionalFilter switches off when about 30% of rows pass.
- Noise: q04/q08/q17 ±5-15%; q16 threshold ~7.9%, q18 ~5%, q13 ~14%, q09 ~8.6%. Implementer-measured gains are often 2x the official ones, and the official bench may flag regressions on q16/q18 that the implementer reads as noise.
- Testing BF: compare against SET disabled_optimizers='join_filter_pushdown' on TEMP tables.
- Budget is tight (~$4/session): read memory/ledger tail, then dispatch the next prior win quickly.
